subject: remove restriction enzyme recognition sequences prior to gl2fasta

messages.author: 9bab4c98a6acda91
messages.subject: remove restriction enzyme recognition sequences prior to gl2fasta
parts:
Hi Arthur,

I've been using the gl2fasta function to produce a single concatenated sequence per individual, with the intention of using these as haplotypes for ML phylogenetic analyses. However, I've realised that these haplotypes contain the restriction enzyme recognition sequences for each locus as well - I was wondering if there's a way to remove these before concatenating each sequence? 

Cheers,
Shandiya

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: remove restriction enzyme recognition sequences prior to gl2fasta
parts:
Hi Shandiya,

You need to ask Diversity Arrays Technology to provide the trimmed sequences when you request your report.

Without them, you should have got an error message.

"Fatal Error: Data must include Trimmed Sequences for each loci in a column called 'TrimmedSequence' in the @other$loc.metrics slot.\n"
 
If you did not get such an error, then the sequences being concatenated should have had the adaptors removed.

If I have misunderstood you, and you are referring to the common restriction enzyme site at the beginning of each fragment, then those should be left there as they are present in the genome along with the rest of the sequence tag.

Hope this helps.

A

messages.author: d87216285ace7535
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: remove restriction enzyme recognition sequences prior to gl2fasta
parts:
On Mon, May 27, 2019 5:12 pm, Arthur Georges wrote:
>
> If you did not get such an error, then the sequences being concatenated
> should have had the adaptors removed.

Meaning, the script automatically removes any potential adaptor sequence
present and removes any loci which lack a snp after adaptor removal.

Cheers
Peter
